events.line: A coach party from Barnsley descends, all hungry, all wanting to know if the peas are mushy. They are. Double takings.
A storm takes the power out for the day. You sell nothing and eat the leftovers by torchlight.
The gulls get at the queue. Customers leave quicker than the chips do.
A man with a notebook orders cod and chips and says 'hm' four times. Word gets around: a good day.
A summer bank holiday. The queue goes round the corner and stops to ask what the queue is for.
The Illuminations are on and the whole prom is hungry. You run out of paper twice.

upgrades.name: A second fryer
upgrades.text: Twice the chips an hour, and twice the oil to heat.

upgrades.name: A long lease on the unit
upgrades.text: A landlord who cannot put the rent up and a council that has noticed.

upgrades.name: A neon sign you can see from the prom
upgrades.text: Visitors find you from half a mile away. So do the electricity bills.

asks.title: The Illuminations
asks.text: The Illuminations are on, and half of Lancashire has come to look at the lights along the front. {deed} is on the way to all of them.

options.label: Open late and put chips in cones for the walk
options.say: Cones of chips by the thousand. The sea wind does the rest.

risk.say: The wind takes the cones, the sauce and your hat.

options.label: Keep the usual hours and the usual queue
options.say: Steady all week. The lights are very pretty and the takings are not bad.

options.label: Shut early, the lights make you tired
options.say: The lights go on without you.
